pr_title: SysfsPath: Have CSysfsPath::Get() return a std::optional because reads can fail
pr_body:
## Description
Reading from sysfs can fail with errors, this causes `CSysfsPath::Get()` to throw an exception. This exception wasn't handled in `CCPUInfoLinux::GetCPUFrequency()` causing Kodi to crash. This PR handles exceptions inside `CSysfsPath::Get()` and returns a `std::nullopt` in case the read failed.

## Motivation and context
Should fix #21747.

## How has this been tested?
In `CCPUInfoLinux::CCPUInfoLinux()` changed the path from `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq` to `/sys/devices/system/cpu/power/autosuspend_delay_ms` which causes an input/output error on my machine:
```
$ cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/power/autosuspend_delay_ms
cat: /sys/devices/system/cpu/power/autosuspend_delay_ms: Input/output error
```
Without this PR Kodi crashes, with this PR it's fine.

## What is the effect on users?
Fixes crash in some circumstances (see #21747)

issue_context.title: Kodi crashes if current freq of CPU 0 is not available
issue_context.body:
<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
<!--- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->
<!--- A bug report that is not clear will be closed -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Kodi crashes upon opening the CPU info page in Settings if it can't read from _/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq_ on Linux.

In short, there are systems with multiple CPUs where disabling some of the CPUs is favorable. On older kernels reading from the _/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuX/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq_ of the disabled CPU was returning simply zero or last known value. Currently it returns _read error_ and that causes Kodi to crash. 

Please read more information here:
https://github.com/LibreELEC/LibreELEC.tv/issues/6758


## Expected Behavior
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Kodi doesn't crash.


## Actual Behavior
<!--- Tell us what happens instead -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Kodi crashes.


## Possible Fix
<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix or reason for the bug -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
Don't expect the CPU 0 to be the main CPU and to be always online. Before trying to read from _/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/scaling_cur_freq_ we should check whether the CPU 0 is actually online by reading _/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/online_. If it is not online, then try CPU 1, 2, 3 etc. until we find CPU which is online and then read all the CPU info from it.


### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
<!--- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to -->
<!--- reproduce this bug. Include code to reproduce, if relevant -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
1. run "_echo '0' > /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/online_"
2. open "Settings" -> "System information" -> "CPU"
3. Kodi crashes on affected platforms (depends on the Linux kernel)
